items.followUp: How many significant figures are in the measurement 0.0450 m?

rubric.why: The definition includes the reliably known digits and the first estimated digit.
rubric.description: Defines significant figures as the reliably known digits plus the first estimated digit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the known digits and the estimated digit.

rubric.why: The answer must give a measurement example and correctly state its significant-figure count.
rubric.description: Gives an example measurement and states its correct number of significant figures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example with the correct count.

modelAnswer: Significant figures are the reliably known digits in a measurement plus the first estimated digit.
For example, 12.3 cm has 3 significant figures.

items.followUp: State the direction of the centripetal force on a body moving in a circular path and contrast it with centrifugal force.

rubric.why: Centripetal force is directed radially inward, toward the centre of the circular path.
rubric.description: States that centripetal force acts toward the centre of the circular path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the force and its inward direction.

rubric.why: Centrifugal force is described as directed away from the centre, opposite to centripetal force.
rubric.description: States that centrifugal force acts away from the centre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the force and its outward direction.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force acts toward the centre of the circular path.
Centrifugal force acts away from the centre, opposite to centripetal force.

items.followUp: Define stable equilibrium and give one example.

rubric.why: In neutral equilibrium, a slight displacement leaves the body in its new position; the height of its centre of gravity remains unchanged.
rubric.description: Defines neutral equilibrium as a body remaining in its new position after a slight displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body remains in its new position; the unchanged centre-of-gravity height is also acceptable supporting detail.

rubric.why: A ball resting on a horizontal surface is a standard example of neutral equilibrium.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of neutral equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a ball or sphere on a horizontal surface or plane.

modelAnswer: A body is in neutral equilibrium if, after a slight displacement, it remains in its new position; the height of its centre of gravity remains unchanged.
Example: a ball resting on a horizontal surface.

items.followUp: Find the horizontal component of a 40 N force making an angle of 60° with the X-axis.

rubric.why: For an angle measured from the X-axis, the vertical component is F sin θ.
rubric.description: Uses the correct formula for the vertical component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the vertical component as F sin θ.

rubric.why: Substitution and evaluation give 50 sin 30° = 25 N.
rubric.description: Substitutes the given values and obtains the vertical component as 25 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct calculation and answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 50 N, θ = 30° (in SI units).
Answer: The vertical component of the force is 25 N.
